record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: In the standard Borel space SB of separable Banach spaces, besides the isomorphism class of ell_2, is there another example of a single isomorphism class that is itself a Borel subset of SB?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $SB$ denote the standard Borel space of separable (infinite-dimensional) Banach spaces, defined as follows: fix an isometrically universal separable Banach space (for example $C([0,1])$), endow the set $F(C([0,1]))$ of its closed subsets with the Effros-Borel structure, and let $SB \subseteq F(C([0,1]))$ be the Borel subset consisting of those closed subsets that are linear subspaces. For a separable Banach space $X$, write $[X] \subseteq SB$ for its linear-isomorphism class, i.e. the set $\{Y \in SB : Y \cong X\}$.

It is known that $[\ell_2]$ is a Borel subset of $SB$. The problem is to determine whether there exists a separable Banach space $X$, not isomorphic to $\ell_2$, such that the isomorphism class $[X]$ is also a Borel subset of $SB$.
artifact.category_tag: Descriptive set theory of Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that G. Godefroy proved that the isomorphism class of $\ell_p$ in $SB$ is Borel for every $1 \le p < \infty$, providing examples beyond $\ell_2$. Thus the question (whether some other isomorphism class besides that of $\ell_2$ is Borel) has been answered affirmatively. Subsequent work (e.g. Kurka and others) has further investigated the Borel/non-Borel complexity of isomorphism classes (showing for instance that the class of $c_0$ is not Borel).

status_evidence.title: Polish spaces of Banach spaces: complexity of isometry and isomorphism classes
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of complexity of isomorphism classes in the standard Borel space of separable Banach spaces; references Godefroy's result that isomorphism classes of $\ell_p$ are Borel.
status_evidence.claim: Godefroy showed that the isomorphism class of each $\ell_p$ is a Borel subset of SB, giving examples other than $\ell_2$.

status_evidence.title: The isomorphism class of c_0 is not Borel
status_evidence.snippet: Kurka shows that the isomorphism class of $c_0$ in SB is not Borel, in contrast to the Borel classes of $\ell_p$.
status_evidence.claim: Some separable Banach spaces (e.g. $c_0$) have non-Borel isomorphism class, while $\ell_p$ classes are Borel.
